notes: Audited against Engrossed-in-House (EH) source text (57 lines, full read). The analysis is a faithful, near-verbatim representation of a 2-section repeal bill: short title (both citation names), repeal of the Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 (D.C. Law 24-345), revival of prior law 'as if such Act had not been enacted', and the two subsection (b) carve-outs (subtitle S of title I, sec. 5-365.01 et seq.; subtitle A of title I, sec. 5-125.01 et seq. and sec. 5-302) are all sourced verbatim. NO material errors and NO material omissions: every operative provision is covered. Five minor unsupported/framing rows, none escalated: (1) top_lines[0].subs[2] and (2) Section 2 detail assert the bill 'uses/exercises Congress's [constitutional] authority over the District of Columbia' — the bill text nowhere states this (the enacting clause is the generic federal form); it is a structurally-defensible but textually-unsourced legal gloss; (3) gaps[1] 'repeals the act outright' is imprecise given the two carve-outs (analysis elsewhere correctly says 'most'); (4)-(5) likelihoodReason's Senate 60-vote and 'unified Democratic opposition' points are standard speculative likelihood framing not in the bill source. Sponsor (R-GA, 29 cosponsors) and House passage are structural metadata permitted by rubric class 8 (House passage also confirmed verbatim in source: 'Passed the House of Representatives November 19, 2025.'). CR quotes (criticisms, featured_quotes) were not audited — the bill text is the only registered source and contains no Congressional Record content.
